P2 dining room furnished in parts/room-12.mjs: a two-cell spruce table at z15 (x28..29) in the door's view, a stair chair at (28,14) and one at (30,15), a standing lantern and a flower pot on the top, and a hanging lantern at (29,6,14) over the lane.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines for this part; light at the feet is 11–12 on all 4 floor cells, none dark.
Walkability is not confirmed: in this copy `room` reports UNREACHABLE because the door and the house shell are still stubs, so the flood never gets in.

waste.what: Placed the table by hand (fence legs and top slabs with g.set) because table_set refuses when a chair stands past its end cell; I checked the chairs and lantern with g.set too, not layers().
waste.cost: about 4 set calls and one retry of the design after the table_set clear-end rule
waste.tool: table_set should accept an explicit clear-end list (or ignore a stair chair that the caller places), or the plan's ROOMS entry should name the table layout so the furnisher isn't guessing about clear ends.

waste.what: Walk check can only pass in the merged build: `$MCD room` in a single-part copy reports every floor cell unreachable because the door and shell from other parts are stubs, so the walk verdict needs the full build to judge.
waste.cost: one room check run that tells nothing about walkability, plus a manual read of the plan grid to confirm the lane by eye
waste.tool: `mcd room` could take a --through option (treat the doorway cells as open air or flood from the neighbouring room) for parts built in isolation, or `mcd plan` could report the lane cells it expects to be open.
